title: QA
lede: How /qa runs the real app, uses the changed parts the way a user would, and fixes what breaks.

setup.name: Set up
setup.role: Pick the surfaces the diff touches and start the app as the repo documents it.
details: The working tree must be clean, so each fix can be its own commit.
Skipped, with a one-line reason, when the change has no runtime entry point.

more: Browser pages, API endpoints, CLI commands, background jobs.

details: Readiness is polled, never waited on with a fixed sleep.
Only seeded or synthetic data; never production.

probe.name: Probe
probe.role: Run each entry point like a user, including bad input, and capture evidence.
details: Each issue gets an ID (QA-001), a severity, exact repro steps, and expected versus actual.
risks: A surface that could not be reached is marked blocked, never counted as passed.

triage.name: Triage
triage.role: Sort issues by severity and pick the ones the fix tier covers.
details: Issues below the tier, in third-party code, or needing infrastructure changes are deferred.
With --report-only, it stops here and writes the report.

fixloop.name: Fix loop
fixloop.role: Fix each issue at its root cause with a failing regression test first, then re-run the probe.
details: Each verified fix is committed with its test as fix(qa): QA-NNN.
A CSS-only defect may use a before/after screenshot instead of a test.
risks: It stops and reports after two reverts, an edit to an unrelated file, 30 fixes, or when fixes keep spreading across many files.
qs: Why does a QA fix need a failing regression test before the fix?

final.name: Final pass
final.role: Re-run every probe near a fix, plus the happy path on each surface.

report.name: QA report
report.role: A table of issues with status and commit, plus one summary line for the PR.
details: Deferred and blocked items are listed with reasons.
Inside the feature chain it writes qa-report.md; standalone it prints in chat.

surface.d: A way users reach the app: page, API, command or job.

blocked.d: Could not be reached; never counted as passed.

regression.d: An automated test that catches the bug if it comes back.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand how scaffold's /qa skill checks that a change really works for a user.
